match.reason: None of the bank points teaches stem cells, self-renewal, differentiation, or totipotent and pluripotent potency; the closest, mitosis and cloning, cover cell division and genetic identity, which are related but different ideas.

draft.title: Stem cells
card: A stem cell can renew itself by dividing to make more stem cells. It can also differentiate, which means it becomes a specialised cell with a particular job.
a cell that can become any cell type, including the cells of the placenta. A fertilised egg and the first few cells it makes are totipotent.
a cell that can become most cell types in the body, but not the placenta. Cells in an early embryo, after the totipotent stage, are pluripotent.
Cells differentiate because different genes are switched on in different cells. The cell's DNA does not change.
draft.remember: Stem cells renew themselves and differentiate. Totipotent cells can become any cell, pluripotent cells can become most.

a.q: Which pair of abilities makes a cell a stem cell?
opts: It renews itself and differentiates into specialised cells
It copies its DNA and keeps the same job in every cell
It divides by binary fission and makes identical cells
It differentiates once and then cannot divide again
a.why: A stem cell can divide to make more stem cells and can also become a specialised cell. The option about keeping the same job is wrong because stem cells can change into cells with different jobs.
a.clue: One ability keeps the supply of stem cells going. The other gives cells a job.

b.q: Researchers grow a cell that can form nerve, muscle and blood cells, but cannot form the placenta. How should the cell be described?
opts: Pluripotent, because it can become most cell types
Totipotent, because it can become many cell types
Pluripotent, because it can become only one cell type
Totipotent, because it can become the placenta only
b.why: The cell can form most body cells but not the placenta, so it is pluripotent. Totipotent is tempting because the cell makes many types, but a totipotent cell could also form the placenta.
b.clue: Check whether this cell can become every cell type, or only most.

a.best: It renews itself and differentiates into specialised cells

b.best: Pluripotent, because it can become most cell types
